question:
A 55-year-old female with a history of chronic alcohol use disorder presents with severe abdominal
pain. Her medical history includes peptic ulcer disease. Physical examination is challenging as the
patient refuses abdominal palpation due to the intensity of the pain. The provider suspects
spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. Which of the following findings would most strongly support this
diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Pain that improves with movement (B) Gentle pressure at the
costovertebral angle elicits pain (C) McBurney's point tenderness (D) Absent bowel sounds (E) Shifting
dullness on percussion (F) Murphy's sign positive (G) Guaiac positive stool (H) Cullen's sign present (I)
Rebound tenderness on light palpation (J) Forced cough elicits abdominal pain
 A. Shifting dullness on percussion
B. Absent bowel sounds
C. Forced cough elicits abdominal pain
D. Cullen's sign present
E. McBurney's point tenderness
F. Gentle pressure at the costovertebral angle elicits pain
G. Murphy's sign positive
H. Rebound tenderness on light palpation

I. Pain that improves with movement
J. Guaiac positive stool
